issues.display_title: Issue #671: Door-based building connectors and Access parent-child controls
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT

Branch: design/door-based-building-connectors

Context

Cross-building directions need to know where a visitor leaves one building and enters another. Today that is modelled as an Access type called Entrance, even though Access objects are otherwise used for vertical circulation (lifts and stairs). Doors are the real objects visitors walk through, so cross-building routing should read normal Door objects instead.

At the same time the Access workflow is split: the Object List does not only inspect objects, it also edits Access type and floor span. That configuration belongs in the selection section above the toolbar, where every other selected-object control already lives.

Docs: docs/superpowers/PRD/2026-08-12-door-access-for-cross-building-directions/prd.md · brief.md

Scope

In scope

  1. Remove Entrance from Access creation and type-editing controls (Lift and Stair only).
  2. Use all existing Door types as cross-building direction connectors.
  3. Keep legacy Entrance markers readable as routing fallback.
  4. Move Access type + floor-connection controls from the Object List to the selection section.
  5. Show Type, Downstairs and Upstairs when a parent Access object is selected.
  6. Auto-create child Access objects when connected floors are selected; delete them when removed.
  7. Show a child Access object as derived, with a View parent action.
  8. Let parent Information links propagate to child Access objects.

Out of scope

  1. Converting legacy Entrance markers into doors automatically.
  2. Auto-detecting or labelling exterior-only doors.
  3. Adding a Door Access type, status, toggle or badge.
  4. Redesigning all selected-object toolbar controls.
  5. Letting child Access objects be independently edited, linked or deleted.

Product rules

Access objects represent vertical movement only — Lift and Stair. Entrance appears in no creation control, type control, selected-object toolbar, Object List control or new-object UI.

Object List shows name, type and delete (where allowed). No type picker, no floor-span editor, no Downstairs/Upstairs editor, no child link/unlink control.

Parent selection section shows Type (Lift / Stair), Downstairs (levels below the parent, ordered downward, plus Not connected) and Upstairs (levels above, ordered upward, plus Not connected). Both directions accept multiple floors; labels may adapt to type (Down lift / Up lift, Down stair / Up stair).

Child selection section shows a read-only parent summary and View parent — no type, floor, Information, group-delete or membership editing. View parent switches to the parent's level and selects it.

Parent resolution: stored origin/parent metadata → earliest createdAt → first member in stored level order.

Door connectors: the route planner discovers usable doors from the building's existing door objects and picks the best door pair by path cost. A door keeps its existing type, geometry, swing and Information behaviour — no new type, role, toggle or badge.

Information links: only a parent can be linked or unlinked in editor Map mode; children inherit the parent's Information and show no separate Not linked state. In Preview and Live, parent and child are each searchable, clickable and routable, sharing the parent's Information.

Legacy Entrance fallback: kept readable for old projects and usable by routing when no door connector is available, but never offered for new authoring and never treated as a vertical connector.

Direction behaviour

  • Same building, same floor — unchanged.
  • Same building, different floors — continues to use Lift and Stair Access objects; parent and child are both valid route endpoints.
  • Different buildings — existing Door objects first, legacy Entrance markers only when no usable door exists. Walk to a door in the origin building → walk outside → enter through a door in the destination building. If a building has neither, directions name the building that needs a door.

Acceptance checklist

  • Entrance is removed from user-facing Access creation controls.
  • Entrance is removed from user-facing Access type editing controls.
  • Access objects remain Lift and Stair only for new authoring.
  • All existing Door types can be used for cross-building directions.
  • No new Door Access type, status, toggle or badge is added.
  • Door connector behaviour does not change door geometry, swing or Information behaviour.
  • Access Object List shows only name, type and delete action.
  • Access Object List does not edit type or connected floors.
  • Parent Access selection shows Type, Downstairs and Upstairs controls.
  • Downstairs shows only levels below the parent level, in order.
  • Upstairs shows only levels above the parent level, in order.
  • Downstairs and Upstairs support multiple selected floors.
  • Not connected clears a direction.
  • Selecting connected floors creates child Access objects.
  • Removing connected floors deletes child Access objects.
  • Selecting a child shows parent summary and View parent.
  • View parent switches to the parent level and selects the parent.
  • Children cannot edit type, floor connections, deletion or Information link.
  • Parent Information links propagate to children.
  • Editor Map mode links Information only on parent Access objects.
  • Not linked indicators appear only for parent Access objects.
  • Preview and Live can search, click, inspect and route to parent and child Access objects.
  • Cross-building directions use normal Door objects.
  • Cross-building directions can still use legacy Entrance markers as fallback when no usable door exists.
  • Legacy Entrance markers are not treated as vertical connectors.
  • Missing building access messages name the building that needs a door.
  • Existing projects with legacy Entrance markers load without data loss.
  • No new Entrance access markers are created by the UI.

Manual verification

  1. Open a multi-floor project; confirm the Access tool offers Lift and Stair only.
  2. Select a parent Access object; confirm the Object List shows only name, type and delete, and the selection section shows Type, Downstairs and Upstairs.
  3. Select multiple Downstairs and Upstairs floors; confirm child Access objects appear on those floors.
  4. Remove one selected floor; confirm the matching child is deleted.
  5. Select a child; confirm only the parent summary and View parent appear, and View parent navigates correctly.
  6. Link the parent to Information in Map mode; confirm children inherit it and show no Not linked state.
  7. Confirm Preview and Live can find and route to both parent and child objects.
  8. Open a multi-building project with normal doors in both buildings; confirm cross-building directions use those doors with no Door Access type or toggle.
  9. Open a legacy project with Entrance markers and no usable door; confirm directions still work through the fallback.
